column1: # Game profile of Batman: Arkham Asylum, base game 1.0.0 (v0), SDK 14.3.0: Rocksteady's Unreal Engine 3 on NVN, FMOD on an AudioOut, Bink movies. Generated by scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py
# (dm/games/profile_guess.py), then brought up on the Mac and played on an iPhone / iPad; the note (README.md) says what each key is for.
# The profile ships no shader tables: the NSP script makes them from the game files, in a profile derived from this one beside the build (derive_profile)
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# Unreal Engine 3 writes its textures into their pools from the CPU after creating them, with no NVN flush: without both keys the 3D scene is black
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the host raises Unreal Engine 3's tick limit (MaxSmoothedFrameRate, [GEngine]+0x758) to fps_target (hle_fpslock.c); the game steps by real time.
# Its window keeps the present interval 2 it was built with, which present_interval display ignores.
# fps_max 120: the launchers' Frame rate offers 120 on the Mac and the engine's limit follows the frames that fit (120 or 60), and Uncapped (DM_FPS_TARGET=unlimited) writes the
# limit out of the way (1000) and free-runs presentation. The game steps by the time that really passed (GUseFixedTimeStep is 0), so its speed holds at 120: 60, 120 and Uncapped were
# The launchers' Render scale: the host fixes the engine's dynamic resolution (Min/MaxScreenPercentage, [[GEngine]+0x4e8]+4) at DM_RENDER_SCALE (hle_fpslock.c);
# Resolution picks the view: 1920x1080 docked, 1280x720 handheld (SwitchApp::OnOperationModeChanged)
# the rewritten modules are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory (Age of Calamity: 66.6 MB → 72 MB)
